title: Photodegradable Hydrogel Interfaces for Bacteria Screening, Selection, and Isolation
protocol: Streak colonies of B. subtilis on ATGN agar plates supplemented with 100 µg/mL spectinomycin.
Streak colonies of E. coli on ATGN agar plates supplemented with 100 µg/mL ampicillin.
Pick desired colonies from ATGN agar plates and start overnight cultures in ATGN liquid medium at 37 °C while shaking at 215 rpm for 24 h.
Store the cell cultures in 50% glycerol at -80°C until future use.
Pick colonies of B. subtilis and E. coli from glycerol stocks using sterile inoculation loops.
Incubate picked colonies in ATGN liquid media for 24 h at 37 °C and 215 rpm.
Prepare media with 2x nutrients for the bacterial strain.
Add phosphate (NaH2PO4) to the medium to achieve a final concentration of 100 mM.
Adjust the pH value of the medium to 8 using 5 M NaOH (aq).
Sterilize the prepared buffer solution and store it at -20°C.
For each mg of PEG-o-NB-diacrylate powder, add 3.08 µL of ultrapure water to reach a concentration of 49 mM.
Vortex the PEG-o-NB-diacrylate solution until well mixed and store at -20°C.
For 4-arm PEG-thiol preparation, add 4 µL of ultrapure water per mg powder to achieve a 20 mM concentration.
Vortex the 4-arm PEG-thiol solution until well-mixed and store it at -20°C.
Place up to 5 glass slides (25 mm x 75 mm x 1 mm) inside a polypropylene slide mailer.
Sonicate the slides with a 2% (w/v) detergent solution for 20 minutes.
Rinse the slides three times with ultrapure water.
Sonicate the slides in ultrapure water for another 20 minutes.
Dry the slides using a stream of N2.
Plasma clean both sides of the glass slides according to protocol for 2 min.
Place plasma-cleaned slides back into slide mailer.
Fill container with a 0.5% (v/v) solution of trichloro(1H, 1H, 2H, 2H-perfluorooctyl)silane in toluene.
Allow glass slides to be functionalized for 3 h at room temperature.
Rinse slides within the slide mailer first with toluene and then ethanol (three times each).
Dry each functionalized slide with a stream of N2.
Place 18 mm x 18 mm coverslips in a Petri dish.
Place Petri dish in plasma cleaner chamber and switch on power.
Turn vacuum pump on until pressure gauge reads 400 mTorr.
Open metering valve to let air into the chamber until steady pressure (800-1000 mTorr).
Select RF with "Hi" mode and expose coverslips for 3 min.
Turn off RF mode and vacuum pump after 3 min.
Take Petri dish out of chamber, flip coverslips.
Place coverslips back in the chamber to plasma clean the other side.
Repeat steps to plasma clean untreated side of glass coverslip.
Remove the Petri dish from the chamber.
Turn off the plasma cleaner.
Turn off the vacuum pump.
Clean and hydroxylate glass coverslips with piranha solution.
Place a clean 100 mm x 50 mm glass dish on a hotplate magnetic stirrer under a fume hood.
Add 14 mL of H2SO4 to the glass dish.
Gently place a small teflon-coated magnetic stir bar inside the dish using teflon-coated forceps.
Turn the stirrer slowly to avoid splashing of the acid.
Gently add 6 mL of H2O2 to the dish.
Allow the solution to become well mixed.
Turn off the stirrer.
Remove the stir bar from the dish using the forceps.
Gently place the coverslips inside the dish using the forceps.
Set the temperature to 60–80 °C.
Gently remove the coverslips using the forceps after 30 min.
Submerge the coverslips in deionized water two times.
Store the coverslips in DI water at RT until further use.
Turn off the hotplate and allow the piranha solution to cool.
Place the glass dish containing the cooled piranha solution in a larger, empty glass beaker.
Add 1 L of water to dilute the piranha solution.
Slowly add sodium bicarbonate powder to neutralize the solution.
Check the pH with pH paper when bubbling stops to verify neutralization.
Pour the neutralized and cooled solution down the sink.
Prepare a 5% (v/v) solution of 269 mM MPTS in dry toluene.
Add 10 mL of the solution to individual 50 mL conical centrifuge tubes.
Place one cleaned coverslip in each tube and submerge it within the solution.
Add 12.5 µL of the crosslinking buffer to an 0.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 5.6 µL of PEG-o-NB-diacrylate solution to the mixture in the microcentrifuge tube.
Add 6.9 µL of 4-arm PEG-thiol solution to the mixture in the microcentrifuge tube.
Initiate the crosslinking reaction by adding the 4-arm PEG thiol to the mixture.
Use the hydrogel precursor solution immediately after mixing for cell encapsulation.
Inoculate the crosslinking buffer with the desired cell density before step 6.1.1.
Place the thiolated base coverslip on a clean Petri dish.
Place two spacers on opposing sides of the coverslip.
Fix the spacers to the base coverslip by taping them to the Petri dish.
Pipette the desired volume of precursor solution onto a non-reactive perfluoroalkylated glass slide.
Place the perfluoroalkylated glass slide on the base coverslip.
Wait 25 min at room temperature for hydrogel formation to complete.
Gently remove the perfluoroalkylated glass slide after gelation.
Place the substrate in a 60 mm x 15 mm Petri dish in specified culture media.
Culture B. subtilis or E.coli for 24 h at 37 °C in ATGN media supplemented with appropriate antibiotics.
Prepare the hydrogel precursor solution by adding 5.6 µL of PEG-o-NB-diacrylate with 12.5 µL of pH 8 phosphate-buffered saline and mixing with 6.9 µL of four-arm PEG thiol solution.
Pipette 12.5 µL of the precursor solution on a non-reactive, perfluoroalkylated glass slide.
Place two 38 µm steel spacers on opposing sides of the microwell array substrate inoculated with cells.
Invert the perfluoroalkylated glass slide with the precursor solution droplet and place it in the middle of the microwell substrate.
Incubate for 25 min at room temperature for hydrogel formation.
Gently remove the glass slide from the microwell substrate.
Tape a stack of ten 18 x 18 mm coverslips together.
Glue this stack of coverslips to the bottom of a Petri dish.
Mix PDMS precursor and curing agent at a ratio of 10:1 volume in a plastic cup.
Degas the mixture in a vacuum desiccator.
Pour the mixture into the Petri dish.
Cure PDMS for 90 minutes at 80°C.
Cut around the taped block to remove the PDMS holder.
Place the PDMS holder on a glass slide for easier handling for microscopy.
Cut 20 cm of PTFE tubing with an inner diameter of 0.05 inches.
Attach one end of the tubing to a 100 µL microliter syringe.
Turn on the microscope (see Table of Materials).
Turn on the patterned illumination tool (see Table of Materials).
Turn on the 365 nm LED light source Analog and Digital control module.
Turn on the LED light source control module.
Open the microscope software.
Open the software for the patterned illumination tool.
Select the Load button in the hardware configuration window.
Press the Start button.
The light patterning software window will open.
Select the Device Control button from the left sidebar of the window.
Calibrate the patterned illumination tool.
Set the microscope objective to 10x magnification.
Place the calibration mirror under the microscope.
Press the LED Control tab in the Device Control window.
Turn on LED #1 and set the light intensity to 60%.
Press the tab titled with the patterned illumination tool product name.
Press the Show Grid button.
Adjust the microscope focus and camera exposure for high image quality of the grid.
Rotate the camera to align the grid lines parallel to the camera window frame if needed.
Select the Calibration Wizard button under the tab titled with the patterned illumination tool product name.
Follow the instructions provided by the software in this window.
Follow the software instructions when the Pre-calibration Adjustment window opens.
Press the Next button.
Save the calibration in the desired folder by entering the date, microscope name, objective lens, and filter when the Mapping Information window opens.
Press the Working Area Definition button under the tab titled with the patterned illumination tool product name to define the working area if needed.
Press the Sequence Design button on the left-sidebar of the software window.
Press the Profile Sequence Editor button.
Select the New Profile option under the Profile List in the Profile Sequence Editor window.
Choose different pattern shapes and sizes or manually draw the pattern for light exposure as desired.
For circle patterns, define a circle with a 30 µm diameter over a target bacteria colony to cover the whole colony.
Choose the shape fill color white.
For broken cross patterns, choose the rectangle shape from the pattern drawing window with 3 µm x 8 µm dimensions.
Place four rectangles on the edges of the target colony, ensuring half the patterns have an overlay with the colony.
Draw a 10 μm diameter circle around the well perimeter for circle patterns, choose white as the fill color.
For ring patterns, draw a circle of 20 μm diameter, place it over the well and choose white as the fill color.
Draw another circle pattern of 10 μm diameter with black as the fill color and place it around the perimeter of the well.
Edit the pattern based on the desired extraction method to ensure it exists within the working area of the patterned illumination tool.
Place the sample in a PDMS holder and pipette defined media on top to prevent dehydration and provide a carrier solution for released cells.
Replace the media with the calibration mirror.
Adjust the microscope focus to get a sharp image of the colonies within the hydrogel.
Identify a colony of interest through inspection.
Design light patterns while observing colonies inside the sample to test different patterns for cell extraction.
Save the defined pattern after testing.
Select the Session Control section and add the saved sequence under the tab titled with the patterned illumination tool product name.
Choose the option to simulate the pattern to view and adjust for the desired location of exposure.
Adjust sample location to project pattern precisely on targeted area.
Set light intensity to 60% under LED control tab.
Set exposure time to 40 seconds under LED control tab.
Start the exposure process.
Monitor hydrogel degradation in real-time and brightfield mode.
Prevent any movements during light exposure to avoid cross-contamination.
Collect cells using a microliter syringe and microfluidic tubing after 365 nm light exposure.
Change microscope filter to FITC or TRITC to visualize exposed area.
Place the end of tubing upon irradiated spot on sample.
Change microscope filter back to brightfield mode.
Monitor cell retrieval in real-time.
Withdraw released cells carefully using the syringe attached to tubing.
Collect 200 μL of solution containing released cells.
Transfer collected solution into a 1.5 mL centrifuge tube for analysis or plating.
Use DNA purification kit to extract DNA from bacteria isolates.
Follow the manufacturer's specification described in the DNA purification kit handbook up to step 7.
Elute the DNA using 100 µL of Buffer AE instead of 200 µL.
Repeat elution once as described in step 11.1.2.
Measure DNA quality using a UV-Vis spectrophotometer.
Turn on the spectrophotometer and select the dsDNA option.
Lift the pedestal arm and clean the pedestal position with DI water and lint-free wipes.
Pipette 2 µL of AE buffer onto the pedestal position.
Gently bring down the pedestal arm and select Blank on the screen.
Lift the pedestal and clean the pedestal position to remove residual material.
Load 2 µL of sample on the pedestal position.
Bring down the pedestal arm and select Measure button on the screen.
Dilute bacterial suspensions by a dilution factor of 105 using a 96-well plate.
Pipette 10 µL of diluted bacterial suspension.
Spot three times on ATGN plates for each bacteria suspension.
Tilt the plates to spread cells on agar surfaces.
Air-dry ATGN plates containing bacterial suspensions.
Incubate the plates at 37 °C for 48 h.
Count and record the Colony Formation Units (CFUs) numbers.
Count all three spreads of bacterial suspensions on each plate.
